<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerExternalDatasourceRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via datasources.external.refreshCatalog (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/refresh-catalog, selected by route anchor /datasources/:name/external/refresh-catalog), refreshCatalog (sdk, the bare tail of client method datasources.external.refreshCatalog, bound to POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/refresh-catalog))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6df5bc6cf1add8ccb050e42be006f79ff5fdd4c` — the merge of head `654d2d88d94c9d4453e3befc78036e68c70d3984` into base `b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6df5bc6cf1add8ccb050e42be006f79ff5fdd4c && git checkout d6df5bc6cf1add8ccb050e42be006f79ff5fdd4c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6 654d2d88d94c9d4453e3befc78036e68c70d3984 && git checkout -B drift-repro b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6 && git merge --no-ff 654d2d88d94c9d4453e3befc78036e68c70d3984

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b62463f1b1dfdb3fff15c6c7db895470d63071d6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `654d2d88d94c9d4453e3befc78036e68c70d3984`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes-auth-guard.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-type-write-capability.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-federation-read-capability.dogfood.test.ts + packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/api.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/ImportObjectDialog.tsx, packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/external-datasource-service.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/package.json, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/datasource/list-tables.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/datasource/introspect.ts, packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md, the ruling record on #9901 (comment 5353919655), commit 6ce58a735

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the committed changeset; no schema path and no governed path in the file list, so `record-recognisers --paths` defers to that line). Inputs: the PR body, its file list, the net diff of this head against its merge-base with `main` (`6f094645b4`), and the head's check-runs. The rule reviewed against: seeing a datasource's remote structure needs the read capability on every route, writes included; the two write routes that answer introspection require both the read and the write capability, and a caller lacking the read capability gets the read routes' own refusal; the same rule on the MCP federation bridge's import tool.

Check-runs on this head at the time of writing: 31 completed success, 13 skipped, 0 failed; still running: `Test Core (2/8)`, `Test Core (3/8)`, `Test Core (4/8)`, `Test Core (6/8)`, `Test Core (8/8)`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not stand in for them, and the landing waits for every check to be green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/refresh-catalog` and `POST …/external/tables/:remote/import` (`@objectstack/rest`)** — narrowed from {`manage_metadata`} to {`manage_platform_settings`, `manage_metadata`}. Read in the tree: `FEDERATION_REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES.write = [READ, WRITE]`, consumed by `refuseFederationRequest` through `federationCapabilityRefusal`. Status and code are unchanged (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`); the sentence names every capability the caller lacks, the read one first, through the same template the read routes use, so a caller lacking only the read capability is answered on a write route exactly as on a read route. **Correct against the rule.** The three read routes, the ADR-0069 posture arm and the anonymous floor are untouched (`'read'` rows unchanged; the guard's order is authGate, then anonymous, then capability, as before).
2. **Position of the refusal** — unchanged: the capability decision sits inside `refuseFederationRequest`, and every one of the five handlers calls `externalService()` only after that returns `false`. A refused write therefore still looks up no service and runs no service method; the auth-guard test asserts both (`lookups` holds no `external-datasource`, no service method called) and the dogfood file asserts the refused import left no object behind `GET /meta/object/:name`. **Correct.**
3. **MCP `import_object` (`@objectstack/runtime`)** — `federationService(…, 'write')` now asks `federationCapabilityRefusal('write', held)` before `deps.resolveService`, throwing the route's sentence with `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403`. Same rule, same order relative to the service lookup as the route. **Correct.**
4. **MCP `tools/list`** — the pair is carried where `federationPairCallable(ec)` holds, which asks the family's rule per kind over the same held set the per-call gate reads. Outcomes: read only → listed, listing served, import refused 403 (unchanged); both → listed and served; write only → carried neither (changed; previously listed with the import served); neither → carried neither (unchanged). This is the existing listing rule — "listed exactly where some call of the pair can pass" — re-evaluated against the new rule rather than a new listing policy; `wireBridgeTools` in `@objectstack/mcp` is untouched and still registers the pair only on a bridge carrying both members. The bridge tests pin all four envelopes, two of them on the envelope the real `/mcp` door resolves. **Follows the existing rule.**
5. **Public surface widening: `federationCapabilityRefusal` and `type FederationCallKind` exported from `@objectstack/rest`** — necessary: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` imports both, and the package's `exports` map admits only `.` (`dist/index.*`), so there is no narrower address for runtime to reach them; the alternative — a second copy of the rule in runtime — is what the diff exists to remove, and the two constants were already exported for the same consumer. Narrowest shape: the function returns the refusal sentence or `undefined` and takes `(kind, held)` only; the requirement table and the purpose strings stay module-private, so a consumer cannot re-derive a different decision from the exported parts. `held` is typed `readonly unknown[] | null | undefined` and non-arrays read as empty — fail-closed, and a non-string entry matches no capability, so the loose parameter type widens no accept set. **Necessary and narrowest.**
6. **`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`** — comment-only hunk; no row changes (`META_TYPE_WRITE_CAPABILITIES` still has no `external_catalog` row, `META_TYPE_READ_CAPABILITIES.external_catalog` is still `manage_platform_settings`, both pinned by `meta-type-write-capability.test.ts`, whose one title change alters no assertion). The claim the note makes — that the `/meta` write doors answer a receipt, never the stored document — holds against the protocol: `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema` is `{ success, version, seq }`, `PublishMetaItemResponseSchema` `{ success, version }`, `DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema` `{ success, reset?, seq? }`. So no `/meta` write row is owed by the new rule. **Correct.**
7. **`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`** — the `import_object` description and the bridge docblock now state the rule; no behaviour in that package changes. **Correct.**
8. **Tests as evidence** — the crossed case in the auth-guard file is flipped rather than deleted and compares the write routes' status and code to the read route's own answer rather than to a literal, asserts the message names the lacking capability and not the held one, and adds a both-capabilities control that proves the services ran. The bridge file adds the write-only and read-only envelopes beside the both-capabilities control. The dogfood file drives the HTTP door on the composed showcase with permission sets authored at runtime through `/meta/permission`, the read-twin's refusal as the comparator, and the admin reading its own control import `200` through the same door that answers the refused import `404`. **Adequate evidence of the rule at three layers.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/mcp`, with a `**BREAKING**` banner and the `!` title. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, and `none` takes `patch` while a breaking non-protocol change keeps its banner and ADR-0087 disposition. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author writes changes — no key, value, type or default — a capability requirement on an HTTP door and an MCP tool is not authorable protocol. **Consistent.**
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers, line-initial, identical. `yes` is correct for the helper export: the line answers whether the card widens an accept set or expands the public surface, and two new members on the package entry (measured on `exports['.']` → `dist/index.d.ts`) are an expanded public surface, so `no (narrowing)` would have been a false `no`. **Routing:** per `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` (`reviewFace`), a `(narrowing)` arm on either carrier decides the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④, and `yes (narrowing)` is named there explicitly — a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing face's review, which subsumes the declaration face. So the `yes` does not route this PR to a second lane or a second record: the widening is judged in this record (① 5), and the remainder of the diff has no path outside this scope (the narrowing floor is every path outside the prose faces; the only prose-face path is the changeset, read here as the carrier).
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, exactly one marker, in the changeset body beside both declaration lines: no export is removed or narrowed, no key moves, no stored row is rewritten; the remedy is a grant on the caller's permission set and the changeset states it as the migration (FROM write capability alone → TO both, one-line fix). **Right category.** The gate reading it (`check:adr-0087-registration`) sits in a Lint job that has completed green on this head.
- `Skills-docs: none — …` line present, as the `(narrowing)` arm owes. See ③ for a correction to its reason; the disposition stands.
- `@objectstack/client` and the CLI are not moved by the diff and owe no changeset; the changeset's "who sees it" paragraph names the `datasources.external.*` callers, which is what the earlier ruling on this family asked of the SDK surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **MCP scope extension** (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`): accepted. The rule is stated for every route into the family, and the bridge is a door into the same two service operations; leaving it on the previous rule would have re-opened the one-operation-two-admission-policies asymmetry this family's invariant forbids. The extension is implemented by consuming the one exported rule, not by a parallel copy.
- **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json`**: not a prose face (the prose faces are `.changeset`, `content/docs/**`, `apps/docs/**`), so it is within this record's scope. Two items' clauses are rewritten to the rule, each with a `revision` bump and a history entry; no step's expected success changes and the first item's own probes (the two read twins) are unchanged. The history `ref` is the branch name rather than `#PR`; `main` already carries many branch-name refs in these files, so this follows precedent. The `check:platform-checklist` gate runs in a Lint job that has completed green on this head. Accepted.
- **Reproduction through the ablation leg rather than a separate `main` checkout**: the mutation replaced the one write row with the write capability alone, which is the previous rule verbatim, so the red it produced at the three layers is a reading of the previous behaviour; the restore was proved by blob identity and a dist-marker scan. Accepted as the dev's evidence; it is not an input of this record — the gate verdicts are the check-runs above.
- **Reading the validate ruling through commit 6ce58a735**: the card it cites is not readable from this seat; the landing commit's message carries the ruling (option A) and its diff, and the current tree's docblocks quote it. A commit sha in this repository's history is the provenance AGENTS.md accepts. Accepted.
- **`Skills-docs:` reason**: the reason says no doc page states which capability the federation routes require. One does — the 17.2 release page's route table (`content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`) lists the two writes on `manage_metadata`. That page is RELEASE-OWNED and ⛔ never edited in a code PR; the changeset is the input the next release notes compile from, and it is present. The disposition `none` therefore stands; only the stated reason was incomplete. Not a must-fix; no card owed.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay author note.
- No `open_questions` are stated on the PR; its "需要你做的" line is empty by design (the narrowing is declared and reviewed here).

### ④ Design judgment

Judged by reading the tree, not the PR body's account of it.

- **A door that still answers introspection on the write capability alone?** Every resolver of the `external-datasource` service at this head: the five federation routes (all through `refuseFederationRequest`: reads `'read'`, writes `'write'`); the admin spelling (`service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`: `remote-tables` and `object-draft`, every one of its eleven routes behind `DATASOURCE_ADMIN_CAPABILITY = manage_platform_settings`, and it has no import or refresh twin); the MCP pair (through `federationService`); and `runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts`, a boot and timer sweep with no caller. The SDK (`packages/client/src/index.ts`, `datasources.external.*`) and the CLI (`datasource list-tables`, `datasource introspect`) are HTTP clients of the federation routes. The `/meta` doors: `external_catalog` reads sit on the `manage_platform_settings` row and writes answer receipts (① 6). The service's own returns confirm why the writes count: `importObject` returns `{ name, definition, review }` and `refreshCatalog` returns the parsed `ExternalCatalog`. **None found.**
- **Does any door now answer differently for an unknown datasource?** No. The capability decision runs before the service lookup on every route and in the bridge, and its sentence names capabilities only, so a refused caller is answered identically whether or not the name resolves; the service-side `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` relay is reachable only past the gate, as before. The write-only caller that previously reached that relay on the two writes now receives the gate's 403 first.
- **The admin spelling**: unchanged, and the change does not disturb the read twins' equivalence (`remote-tables`/`object-draft` versus `external/tables`/`external/tables/:remote/draft`, both on `manage_platform_settings`).
- **A Studio flow a stock profile loses?** The datasource page's client (`ui/…/external/api.ts`) calls `GET tables`, `POST draft`, `POST refresh-catalog`, `POST validate`, and imports through `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name` (`importObjectDraft`); it never calls `…/tables/:remote/import`. Stock sets: `admin_full_access` (`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES`) holds both `manage_metadata` and `manage_platform_settings`; `organization_admin` holds neither; `member_default`, `viewer_readonly` and the showcase example sets name neither federation capability. So an administrator keeps every step; a read-only profile keeps listing, drafting and validating and is refused the refresh exactly as before (it lacked the write capability already); a write-only profile could not list tables on that page before and is now refused the refresh too — and no stock profile is one. **Nothing lost.**
- **Fail-closed on malformed input**: `held` that is not an array reads as empty and is refused; `kind` is a closed two-member type. The order anonymous → capability is kept, so an anonymous caller is still told it has no identity, not that its empty set is insufficient.
- **One rule, one place**: the REST guard and the bridge both consume `federationCapabilityRefusal`; the only other reading of the two constants is the bridge's `heldFederationCapabilities` filter, which narrows the envelope to the two capabilities before handing it to the rule — harmless, since the rule ignores anything else.

No must-fix found.
